getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.summary: Find your way around {app} and make your first app, whichever way suits you.

body.0: When you sign in you land on your dashboard. You can always get back to it with My apps in the top bar.
body.1: Under Your apps, each app has a card with a small picture of its home page, how many pages and flows it has, and whether it is Live (published) or a Draft (only you can see it). Use All apps, Live and Drafts and the Find an app… box to narrow the list.
body.2: Click the picture on a card to carry on editing. Click the app's name to open its Overview. The line beside Your apps shows your plan, how many apps you have, and how many AI actions you've used this month. Click it to open Billing & plan.

shot.alt: The dashboard, with the idea box at the top and a card for each app below.
shot.caption: Your dashboard. Each card is one of your apps.

1.heading: Six ways to start an app

body.0: Pick whichever suits you. Every way ends with an app you can keep changing in the same tools.

bullets.0: Describe it. Type what you want in your own words. The AI suggests a plan you can check and change, then builds the pages, forms and data.
bullets.1: AI Designer. Chat with the AI and shape your app step by step. See the guide Design with the AI Designer.
bullets.2: Templates. Start from a finished design, like a restaurant or a portfolio, and change every word, picture and colour.
bullets.3: Copy a website. Bring up to 30 pages of a website you own into a new app you can edit.
bullets.4: Blank app. Start with a simple page and build it yourself with drag-and-drop blocks.
bullets.5: Import an app. Bring back an app from a backup .zip file, made on this server or another one.

2.heading: Describe your app and check the plan

body.0: If the AI isn't set up on this server, this way and the AI Designer aren't offered. Start from a template instead.

steps.0: On your dashboard, type a sentence about your app in the box, for example “Bookings for my dog walking business”, and press Plan my app. You can also press More ways to start and use the big box there.
steps.1: Say who uses the app and what they do in it. Stuck? Tap one of the example ideas under the box, then change it.
steps.2: Wait a moment while the AI reads your idea. Nothing is built yet.
steps.3: Check the plan under Here's what I'll build: the app's name, its look (click the colour swatch to pick another), its Pages, What it saves and I assumed. Remove a page you don't want with its bin icon.
steps.4: Want something different? Type it under Want something different?, for example “Add a prices page”, and press Update plan.
steps.5: Press Build my app. It usually takes a few minutes. You can leave the page: the build keeps going and will be there when you come back.
steps.6: When it's ready, your app opens in the page editor with a short welcome.

shot.alt: The new app screen, asking What do you want to make?, with a large text box and example ideas.
shot.caption: Describe your app in your own words. You see a plan before anything is built.

body.0: Templates. Click a template to see it bigger, type a name for your app and press Create app from this template. Use the search box and the category buttons to narrow the list.
body.1: Copy a website. Type the site's address, for example mybusiness.com, and press Copy my site. Only copy sites you own or have permission to use. Press Stop to cancel; nothing is saved.
body.2: Blank app. Type a name and press Create app. You get a simple welcome page with your app's name to build on, plus pages for signing in and signing up.
body.3: Import an app. Choose the backup .zip file, type a new name if you like, and press Import app. You get a copy with its pages, flows, data and pictures. Passwords of the app's own members aren't in backups, so they use Forgot password once.

body.0: Each app has tabs along the top: Overview, Pages, Features, Flows, Data, Notifications, Theme, Domains and Mobile app, with Preview and Publish on the right. Apps made with the AI Designer have a Designer tab instead of Overview.
body.1: The Overview shows whether your app is live and its address, a Launch checklist of the next things to do, a code to scan to open it on your phone, your app icon, the latest things visitors sent you, and email alerts. Continue editing takes you back to your pages.

shot.alt: An app's Overview tab, with the app's name, counts of pages and flows, and the launch checklist.
shot.caption: The Overview: your app at a glance, with a checklist of next steps.

bullets.0: Your work saves as you go. There's no Save button in the page editor.
bullets.1: Nothing is public until you publish. Preview lets you try your app first.
bullets.2: To delete an app, use the bin icon on its card on the dashboard. Download a backup first: deleting can't be undone.
bullets.3: Your plan may limit how many apps you can make. When you reach it, see Billing & plan.
bullets.4: Hold your mouse over a button to see a short tip about it. You can turn tips off in your Profile.

ai-designer.title: Design with the AI Designer
ai-designer.summary: Describe your app in plain words, then shape it by chatting with the AI and clicking on what you want changed.

steps.0: Click Designer in the top bar. On a phone, go to More ways to start on your dashboard and choose Design it together.
steps.1: Under What do you want to make?, describe your app. Say who it's for and what visitors should be able to do, like book a time or send a message. You can also tap one of the example ideas and change it.
steps.2: Press Design it.
steps.3: The AI may ask A few quick questions first. Tap an answer, type your own, or skip any of them. Press Build it, or Skip questions to let the AI decide.

shot.alt: The AI Designer home, with a box to describe your app, example ideas and a list of your designs.
shot.caption: Describe what you want, then press Design it.

body.0: While the AI works, the conversation on the left shows Working on it… with each step as it happens, and the preview on the right fills in. A first design can take a few minutes.
body.1: To stop part-way, press the square stop button next to the message box. Nothing from that run is kept.
body.2: Once the first build is done, your design has its own app. Open app at the top of the conversation takes you to it, where you'll find its data, flows and publishing.

steps.0: Type what you want changed in the Ask for a change box, in your own words. For example: “make the header darker” or “add a page with our prices”.
steps.1: Press Enter, or the send button. Shift+Enter starts a new line.
steps.2: The AI updates the design and saves it as a new version.

shot.alt: A design open in the AI Designer: the conversation on the left and a preview of the app on the right.
shot.caption: The conversation is on the left, the live preview on the right.

3.heading: Point at what you want changed

body.0: Sometimes it's easier to show the AI than to describe it.

steps.0: Press Comment above the preview. It changes to Click anything to comment.
steps.1: Click the part of the preview you want changed.
steps.2: Type what should change, for example “make this bigger”, and press Add. Your note waits above the message box.
steps.3: Add as many notes as you like, then press send to make all the changes at once. To drop a note, press its x.

4.heading: Check every page and screen size

body.0: Use the Page menu above the preview to see each page of your design. The three screen buttons show it at computer, tablet and phone width. The arrow button opens the page on its own in a new tab.
body.1: On a phone, switch between Conversation and Preview at the top of the screen.

5.heading: Go back to an earlier version

body.0: Every change is saved as a version, so you can always go back.

steps.0: Press Versions. Every version is listed, newest first.
steps.1: Press View to show an older version in the preview. You can also press See this version under a message in the conversation.
steps.2: Press Restore (or Restore it in the yellow bar) to make that version the current one. The version you had stays in the list, so you can switch back.
steps.3: To stop looking at an old version, press Back to the current version.

shot.alt: The Versions list open next to the preview, with View and Restore buttons for each version.
shot.caption: Versions: look at any earlier version and bring it back.

6.heading: Download it, or move it to the page builder

body.0: Download saves every page of your design as one .zip file.
body.1: Move to page builder hands the app over to the drag-and-drop page editor. After that the AI Designer can't change it any more. If you want to keep designing with the AI, press Make a copy to keep designing: you get a separate copy, and the app in the page builder stays as it is.

body.0: The Designer home lists Your designs. Click a card to open one. The … button on a card lets you Rename, Make a copy or Delete it.
body.1: Deleting a design also deletes its app, unless the app was moved to the page builder. It can't be undone.

bullets.0: Asking the AI for a design or a change uses your plan's monthly AI allowance, if it has one.
bullets.1: In a Designer app, the pages come from the design. Change them here, not in the page editor.
bullets.2: Your app's data, flows, domains and publishing are on its tabs, the same as any other app. Publish it with the Publish button.

game-studio.title: Make a game in the Game Studio
game-studio.summary: Describe a game and the AI builds a real, playable game step by step, which you can play as it grows and change by chatting.

steps.0: Click Games in the top bar. On your dashboard you can also choose Make a game.
steps.1: Under What game do you want to make?, describe your game: what the player does, what they collect or avoid, and how it should look. You can also tap one of the example ideas and change it.
steps.2: Choose 2D or 3D, or Let the AI choose. To show the look you want, add pictures with the image button.
steps.3: Press Build it. The AI may ask A few quick questions first. Pick or type answers, then press Build it, or Skip questions.

body.0: The AI first writes a Game plan: the kind of game, how you play, how you win and lose, and the look. It picks matching art and sound from the asset library.
body.1: Under Art direction in the plan you see the look it chose for your game: the colours, the camera, the shapes, the lighting, the interface and the motion. Every step follows it, so the game looks finished from the start.
body.2: Then it builds the game in small steps, shown in the chat with a tick as each one is done. After every step the game on the right updates in place and you can play it straight away: the background first, then the player and controls, the level, things to collect, enemies, menus, sounds and polish.
body.3: Every step is checked before it reaches your game: it must load and play without errors. A step that fails gets one more try.
body.4: After the level, the enemies and the final polish, a playtester checks the game the way a player would: can every jump be made, can the goal and the collectibles be reached, is the start safe, is the player easy to see, do the touch buttons cover anything. It also looks at the game on a computer screen and a phone and checks that everything looks like one finished game. It tells you in the chat what it found. Real problems are fixed in an extra step straight away; smaller ones are fixed in the next step.

body.0: Click the game, then use the keyboard (arrow keys or WASD, Space to jump). On a phone the game shows touch controls.
body.1: The bar above the game shows the step you're looking at and how smoothly it runs. Use the buttons there to pause, restart, switch between a computer screen and a phone, play full screen or open the game in a new tab.
body.2: If the game reports errors, a yellow button shows how many. Click it to see them and press Ask the AI to fix these.

steps.0: Type what you want in the Ask for a change box, for example “make the jump higher”, “add a second level” or “swap the hero for a robot”.
steps.1: Press Enter. The AI plans the change as one or a few steps, and the game updates as each one lands.

body.0: You don't have to wait for a build to finish. Keep typing in the message box while the AI works: ask what it is doing, or ask for a change like “make the hero orange” or “add a jumping frog enemy”. You can add pictures and assets too.
body.1: Your note shows in the chat straight away and the AI answers at once. It reads every note before its next step and puts what you asked ahead of its original plan. If the plan doesn't cover it, a step is added to the list. A note sent during the last step gets an extra step of its own.
body.2: Under each note you can see where it stands, for example Applied in step 3.

steps.0: To stop once the step that's running now is saved, press Stop after this step. Press Keep going if you change your mind.
steps.1: To stop straight away, press Stop now. The step the AI was working on is dropped and your game stays as it was after the last finished step.
steps.2: To undo a finished step, open Versions and restore the version before it.

body.0: Press Assets above the game (on a phone, the Assets tab). Search thousands of sprites, 3D models, sounds and music, and see what your game uses under In this game.
body.1: Drag an asset onto the message box, or press its + button, then say what to do with it, like “use this as the hero”.
body.2: Assets marked Hosted only can be used in games published here but are left out when you download the game.

6.heading: Go back to an earlier version

body.0: Every step is saved as a version with a picture of the game at that point.

steps.0: Press Versions above the game.
steps.1: Press Play to try an older version on the canvas. Your game doesn't change.
steps.2: Press Restore to make it the current version. The version you had stays in the list.

body.0: Publish turns your game into an app with its own web address that anyone can play. From the app you can also make a phone app and add your own domain. After more changes, press Publish again.
body.1: Download saves the game as a .zip that runs on any web host.

bullets.0: Building a game, and each change you ask for, uses one action of your plan's monthly AI allowance, however many steps it takes. If the AI can't deliver anything, it doesn't count.
bullets.1: If the server restarts while your game is being built, the build carries on from the step it was on.
bullets.2: Games are built with real game engines: Phaser for 2D and three.js for 3D.

page-editor.title: Edit your pages
page-editor.summary: Change words, pictures and layout by clicking and dragging, or ask the AI to do it for you.

body.0: Open the Pages tab. On the left are Blocks, Features and Assets (free photos). In the middle is your page. On the right are Design, Layers, Settings and Theme.
body.1: The bar above your page has undo and redo, whether your work is saved, the screen size buttons and Preview. The panel buttons at each end hide or show the side panels when you want more room.

shot.alt: The page editor: blocks on the left, the page in the middle and design settings on the right.
shot.caption: The page editor. Click anything on your page to change it.

body.0: Click any words on the page and type to change them.
body.1: Double-click a picture to swap it for another one. You can also pick a picture and then tap a photo in Assets. Double-click an icon to choose a different icon.

steps.0: Click the part of your page you want the new piece to go under.
steps.1: In Blocks on the left, find what you want. Blocks are grouped, for example Layout, Sections, Content, Forms and Media. Type in Search blocks... to find one fast, like “button” or “photo”.
steps.2: Tap the block to add it below the part you picked, or drag it to exactly where you want it.

body.0: Click something on your page to select it. Its name shows at the top of the right-hand panel, and a small toolbar appears next to it: Select the part around this, Move up, Move down, Drag to move, Duplicate and Delete.
body.1: The Layers tab lists every piece of your page in order. Click a row to select a piece that's hard to click, or drag rows to move pieces. The eye icon hides a piece while you work on the rest.

body.0: Select something and open Design on the right. Change its text, colours, spacing, size and corners, and the page updates straight away.
body.1: Advanced shows more options, like fonts, shadows and how pieces line up inside a box, plus styles for when the mouse is over something. For colours and fonts across your whole app, use Theme.

5.heading: Settings for links, buttons, forms and lists

body.0: Select a link, picture, button, form or list and open Settings on the right. For example:

bullets.0: Goes to sets where a link takes people. Use /page-name for your own pages, or a full https:// address for another site.
bullets.1: Picture description describes a picture for people who can't see it, and for search engines.
bullets.2: When sent, run (on a form) picks the flow that runs when someone sends it. When pressed, run does the same for a button.
bullets.3: Show items from (on a list) picks where the list gets its items, like your bookings or products.

steps.0: Press Ask AI at the bottom right.
steps.1: To change just one part, select it on the page first. The panel then says Changes apply to the selected…. Press Whole page instead to change the whole page.
steps.2: Type what you want, like “add a pricing section”, and press Enter or Send. You can attach a picture too, like a screenshot of a design you like.
steps.3: The page changes in the editor. If you don't like it, press undo.

shot.alt: The AI Assistant panel open over the page editor, with suggested changes to try.
shot.caption: Ask AI: say what to change and it changes the page for you.

body.0: Click the page name at the top, next to EDITING, to see Your pages. Click a page to open it. Your changes on the page you're leaving are saved first.
body.1: To add a page, press Add page, type its name and press Add page again. It shows up in your app's menu.
body.2: Next to each page: the gear opens Page settings (rename it, choose who can see it, its place in the menu, or Duplicate it), the house makes it your home page, and the bin deletes it after you confirm. Deleting a page can't be undone.

8.heading: Check it on a phone, then preview

body.0: The Desktop, Tablet and Mobile buttons show your page at each size. Always check Mobile: most visitors use phones.
body.1: Preview opens the page in a new tab so you can try it, with its buttons and forms working. It shows your latest changes. Visitors don't see them until you publish.

body.0: The curved arrows at the top left undo and redo your last changes, including changes the AI made.
body.1: Your changes save by themselves. The bar shows Saving… and then Saved. If it says Not saved, check your connection: it keeps trying, and Retry tries again straight away. If your changes didn't reach the server before you closed the tab, you'll be offered Restore the next time you open the page.

bullets.0: Changes stay in your draft. Visitors see them after you publish.
bullets.1: Apps made with the AI Designer get their pages from the design, so change them in the Designer.
bullets.2: If a ready-made block asks Wire this up?, Yes, connect it sets up a place to keep what people send and connects the form. No, I'll handle it adds the block as it is.

look-and-feel.title: Colours and fonts
look-and-feel.summary: Pick a ready-made theme, or set your own colours, fonts and corners for every page of your app.

steps.0: Open the Theme tab.
steps.1: Look through Light themes and Dark themes.
steps.2: Click one. The Live preview on the right shows it straight away. Switch between Your home page and Sample to see it on different things.
steps.3: That's it: changes save by themselves, and Saved appears at the top.

shot.alt: The Theme tab with light and dark theme choices on the left and a live preview on the right.
shot.caption: Click a theme and the preview updates straight away.

body.0: Under Customize you can change any part of the theme:

bullets.0: Mode: light or dark.
bullets.1: Body font for normal text and Display font for headings. A sample line shows each one.
bullets.2: Colors: Primary is your main colour, used for buttons and links. Primary hover is the shade when someone points at them; it follows Primary when you change it. Then Accent, Background, Surface and Surface 2 (cards and panels), Border, Text and Text muted.
bullets.3: Corners: Radius for buttons and cards, and Radius sm for small things. 0 is square; bigger numbers are rounder.

body.0: In the page editor, the Theme tab on the right has the same colour and font settings, so you can adjust them without leaving your page.

bullets.0: The theme applies to every page of your app.
bullets.1: Click a colour box to pick a colour, or type a colour code like #3366ff.
bullets.2: Reset puts back the theme you had when you opened the Theme tab.
bullets.3: Visitors see theme changes after you publish.

features.title: Add features
features.summary: Add ready-made parts like bookings, a shop or a blog, complete with their own pages and saved data.

body.0: A feature is a ready-made part of an app, like bookings, a shop, a contact form or a blog. Adding one gives your app new pages, the lists where it keeps what people send, and the flows that make its buttons and forms work. You can then change its pages like any other page.

steps.0: Open the Features tab.
steps.1: Search, for example “bookings” or “shop”, or pick a group like Commerce or Community.
steps.2: To see what a feature adds, open Details on its card. It says how many pages, lists of saved items and flows it adds.
steps.3: Click the card (Add to my app).
steps.4: Answer its few questions, if it has any. Fields marked * must be filled in. Your app's name is filled in for you where it asks for a business name.
steps.5: Press Add to my app. The editor opens on the feature's first page.

shot.alt: The Features tab: a search box, category buttons and a grid of features to add.
shot.caption: Pick a feature. Details shows what it adds.

body.0: In the page editor, the Features tab on the left does the same thing. When the feature is added, a message says its pages are in the menu, with a button to Open the new page.

shot.alt: The Add a feature dialog asking a few questions, with Cancel and Add to my app buttons.
shot.caption: Answer a couple of questions and the feature is added.

3.heading: Where to find what it added

body.0: Its pages are in your app's menu and in the page list in the editor. What it saves (for example bookings) is on the Data tab. Its flows are on the Flows tab. Pages meant only for you, like a list of bookings, are listed on the Overview under Your app's admin area.

bullets.0: A card marked Added is already in your app. Adding it again makes another copy, with its own pages and lists.
bullets.1: If a feature needs another one first, the message offers a button to add that one.
bullets.2: Some features let signed-in visitors send things that wait for your approval. In Places, for example, people suggest a venue under My venues, and it shows in the guide once you approve it on the Manage places page.
bullets.3: Some features send email, and say Needs email to be set up on the server. If email isn't set up, ask whoever runs {app} for you.
bullets.4: There's no one-step remove. You can delete the pages a feature added, like any page; what it saved stays on the Data tab.
bullets.5: Adding a feature changes your draft. Visitors see it after you publish.

forms-and-data.title: Forms and your data
forms-and-data.summary: See, search, change and download everything your app saves, like messages, bookings and sign-ups.

body.0: When someone sends a form, makes a booking or signs up, your app saves it as a row in a table. A table is like a spreadsheet: one row for each entry and one column for each answer. Tables are on the Data tab. The five newest entries also show on your app's Overview under Latest submissions.
body.1: A form saves answers when it's connected to a flow that saves them. Forms that come with features, and forms in apps the AI builds, are already connected. For a form you add yourself, select it in the page editor, open Settings and choose a flow under When sent, run.

steps.0: Open the Data tab.
steps.1: Click a table. Each one shows how many rows it has, or Empty.
steps.2: To go back to the list, press All tables.

shot.alt: The Data tab listing the app's tables, each with its number of rows.
shot.caption: Everything your app saves, one table at a time.

body.0: Type in Search to find rows. Click a column's name to sort by it. When there are lots of rows, use Newer and Older at the bottom.

steps.0: To change one answer, click it, type the new value and save.
steps.1: To change a whole row, press the pencil at the end of it.
steps.2: To add a row yourself, press Add a row.
steps.3: To delete rows, tick them, press Delete (it says how many rows) and then Yes, delete. Press Keep them if you change your mind.

shot.alt: A table open on the Data tab, with a search box, Add a row and Download CSV buttons, and the rows below.
shot.caption: A table: search it, change it, or download it.

body.0: Download CSV saves the table as a file you can open in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets. It downloads what you're looking at, so search or sort first if you only want some rows.

4.heading: Get an email for every new entry

body.0: On your app's Overview, Alerts lists each table that collects things from visitors, with an On and Off switch. Alerts go to your account's email address, and you can add up to three more under Also send to. Press Save alerts, then Send a test to check it works.
body.1: Alerts need email to be set up on the server. If it isn't, the card says so.

body.0: People can ask what your app keeps about them, or ask for it to be deleted. Open Privacy requests on the Data tab to find one person by email or phone number, then Download a copy of their data or Erase it. People who asked to delete their account from your app are listed under Waiting for your approval.

bullets.0: Deleting rows or erasing a person can't be undone.
bullets.1: Some tables can only be viewed here, for example ones kept in a Google Sheet.
bullets.2: Advanced, at the bottom of the Data tab, shows where your data is stored and lets you make new tables by hand. Most people never need it.
bullets.3: A backup from the Publish tab includes every table and row.

flows.title: Automate with flows
flows.summary: Make things happen by themselves when someone uses your app, like saving a booking and emailing you, or run jobs on a schedule.

body.0: A flow is a short list of steps your app follows by itself. Something happens (someone sends a form or presses a button, or it's a set time), your steps run (save the answers, send an email), and your visitor gets a result (a thank-you message).
body.1: Apps the AI builds, and features you add, come with their flows already set up. You can open and change them like any flow.

body.0: The Flows tab lists each flow with how it starts (with a form, with a request, or on a schedule) and how many steps it has. Click one to open it.
body.1: Each flow has an On / Paused switch, on the list and inside the flow. A paused flow doesn't run: anything in your app that uses it, like a form, gets an error instead. Pausing and turning back on apply to your live app straight away, with no need to publish.

shot.alt: The Flows tab listing the app's flows, each with how it starts and its number of steps.
shot.caption: Your app's flows.

steps.0: On the Flows tab, press New flow, type a name like “Submit contact form” and press Create.
steps.1: The flow opens with its start step, When the app calls this.
steps.2: Under Add step on the left, click a step to add it. Type in Find a step… to search. Steps are grouped: Start, Saved data, Decisions and values, Send and connect, AI, Accounts and Finish.
steps.3: Connect the steps in the order they should run: drag from the right edge of one step to the next step.
steps.4: Click a step to set it up in the panel on the right, for example which table to save to.

shot.alt: A flow open in the flow editor: steps to add on the left, connected steps in the middle, settings on the right.
shot.caption: Add steps on the left, connect them, and set each one up on the right.

body.0: Most step settings let you insert values instead of typing fixed text. Under From the request, type the name of a form field, like email, and press Add. From previous steps lists values that earlier steps made, like the record a step found.

steps.0: Open the page in the page editor and select the form or button.
steps.1: Open Settings on the right.
steps.2: For a form, choose your flow under When sent, run. For a button, use When pressed, run. For a list, Show items from picks a flow that finds the items.

body.0: These are the usual shapes. Features set most of them up for you.

bullets.0: Contact form that emails you: When the app calls this, then Add a record (your messages table), then Send an email to yourself with the person's message inserted, then Reply with a thank-you.
bullets.1: Booking: When the app calls this, then Count or add up records to count bookings at that time, then If this, otherwise that. If the time is free, Add a record and Send an email to confirm; if not, Reply that it's taken. The Bookings feature does all this for you.
bullets.2: Sign-in: the Sign-in and accounts feature adds these flows. Signing up uses Protect a password, Add a record and Sign the person in. Signing in uses Find records, Check a password and Sign the person in.
bullets.3: Daily summary: on the Schedule tab choose On a schedule and Every day, then Count or add up records and Send an email with the total.

6.heading: Try it with a test run

body.0: Press Test run to run the flow once, straight away, with your latest changes. The result shows under the steps. It really does its steps, so it saves records and sends emails, and it appears in Activity.

The Activity tab lists each time the flow ran: Went through, Answered, Finished with a problem or Failed. Press Only problems to see just the ones that went wrong, and open a run to see what the person sent.
body.1: Problems also show on your app's Overview under Problems in the last 24 hours, and as a number on the app's card on your dashboard.

shot.alt: The Activity tab of a flow, listing recent runs and whether each went through.
shot.caption: Activity: every run, and what went wrong if something did.

steps.0: Open the flow's Schedule tab.
steps.1: Choose On a schedule instead of When your app uses it.
steps.2: Under How often, pick Every few minutes, Every hour, Every day, Monday to Friday or Once a week, then the time and your time zone.
steps.3: Save, then publish your app. Schedules only run in the published app.

bullets.0: To remove a step, select it and press its bin, or press Delete on your keyboard.
bullets.1: Flow changes are part of your draft. Visitors get them after you publish.
bullets.2: Send an email only sends when email is set up on the server. If it isn't, your app's Overview warns you.
bullets.3: The Ask AI step uses your plan's AI allowance each time it runs.
bullets.4: Pausing or turning a flow back on applies straight away, including its schedule. You don't need to publish.
bullets.5: Some plans don't include scheduled flows. The Schedule tab says so.
bullets.6: Web address (for developers) is only needed to start a flow from outside {app}.

members-and-sign-in.title: Members, sign-in and private pages
members-and-sign-in.summary: Let people make accounts in your app, and choose which pages everyone, signed-in members or only admins can open.

body.0: The Sign-in and accounts feature gives your app Log in, Sign up and Profile pages, and the flows behind them. New apps usually have it already. If yours doesn't, add it from the Features tab.
body.1: People who sign up are members of your app. Their accounts are separate from your own {app} account.

steps.0: In the page editor, click the page name at the top to open Your pages.
steps.1: Press the gear next to the page (Page settings).
steps.2: Under Who can see this page, choose Everyone, Signed-in people (visitors sign in first; anyone can make an account) or Admins only (only you and the people you make admins).
steps.3: Press Save.

shot.alt: The Page settings dialog, with the page's name, who can see it, and its place in the menu.
shot.caption: Page settings: choose who can open the page.

body.0: In Page settings, Show in menu puts a link to the page in your app's menu, and Move up and Move down set its place. The home page always comes first. A page that isn't in the menu can still be opened by anyone with its link, if they're allowed to see it.

On your app's Overview, Your app's admin area lists the pages that are only for you and your team, like a list of bookings. Click one to open it without signing in to your app. Before you publish, they open in Preview.

4.heading: Give your team an admin login

steps.0: On your app's Overview, find Admin logins for your team.
steps.1: Type their Email and a Password of at least 10 characters.
steps.2: Press Add admin. They can now sign in on your app's sign-in page and open its admin pages.

shot.alt: The Your app's admin area card on the Overview, with admin pages and a form to add an admin login.
shot.caption: Open your admin pages, or give someone an admin login.

bullets.0: Using the email of someone who already has an account in your app makes them an admin and changes their password.
bullets.1: If a page is private but your app has no sign-in page yet, only you can open it. Page settings warns you.
bullets.2: Changes to who can see a page are part of your draft. Publish to apply them.
bullets.3: Members can delete their own account. Requests to delete show on the Data tab under Privacy requests.
bullets.4: Members' passwords aren't in backups. After an import, members use Forgot password once.

publishing.title: Publish and share your app
publishing.summary: Put your app online, share its link, update it safely and bring back an earlier version if you need to.

body.0: You always work on a draft. Visitors see the version you last published. Your changes, including the AI's, stay in the draft until you publish again, so nobody sees half-finished pages.

steps.0: Press Publish at the top right of your app's tabs.
steps.1: Press Publish app.
steps.2: You'll see Your app is live. Ready to share. and the status changes to Live.

shot.alt: The Publish tab showing the app's status, the publish button and its web address.
shot.caption: Publish, and copy your app's link to share it.

body.0: Your app's web address is on the Publish tab, with a button to copy it. On the Overview there's a code you can scan with your phone's camera to open it.
body.1: Search and sharing sets the description search engines and chat apps show with your link. Turn on Hide from search engines if you don't want your app listed on Google; anyone with the link can still open it.

body.0: When you've changed something since publishing, the status says Live · you have unpublished changes. Press Publish changes to make them live. When there's nothing new, the button says Up to date.
body.1: Want to try your changes first? Preview, at the top right, opens your draft in a new tab. Only you can open it.

4.heading: Go back to an earlier version

body.0: Every time you publish, the version is kept under Release history, newest first, with the live one marked Live.

steps.0: Find the version you want under Release history.
steps.1: Press Make live and confirm.
steps.2: Visitors see that version straight away. Your draft isn't changed, so you can fix things and publish again.

shot.alt: The Release history list, with a Make live button next to earlier versions.
shot.caption: Release history: bring back any recent version.

body.0: Take offline stops visitors opening your app until you publish again. Nothing is deleted.

6.heading: Back up or move your app

body.0: Download backup (.zip) saves one file with every page, flow, table and row, your theme and your pictures. Keep it somewhere safe, or bring it back with Import an app when you start a new app, here or on another {app} server. Members' passwords aren't included.

7.heading: Install it on computers and phones

body.0: Under Install on devices: Download offline app (.zip) gives a copy that works on one computer without the internet, keeping its data on that computer. Desktop shortcut (online) puts a shortcut to your live app on a Windows or Mac desktop. For phones, see the guide Phone apps and notifications.

bullets.0: Your plan may limit how many apps you can have published at once.
bullets.1: Release history shows your 20 most recent versions.
bullets.2: Scheduled flows only run once your app is published.
bullets.3: You can connect your own web address on the Domains tab.

custom-domains.title: Use your own domain
custom-domains.summary: Put your app on a web address you own, like www.yourbusiness.com.

body.0: You need a domain name you've bought from a domain company, and a way to change its DNS settings. DNS is the address book of the internet: two entries there tell it that your domain belongs to your app. Your domain company's website has a page for it, often called DNS, DNS records or zone.
body.1: Your app keeps its free address too.

steps.0: Open the Domains tab.
steps.1: Type your address, for example www.yourbusiness.com (without https://), and press Add domain.
steps.2: You'll see two records to add: a CNAME (or A) record and a TXT record. Each has a Name / host and a Value / points to. Click a value to copy it.
steps.3: In another tab, sign in to your domain company, open the DNS settings for your domain, and add both records exactly as shown.
steps.4: Come back and press Check now. When both records are found, it says Connected, and visitors can use your address.

shot.alt: The Domains tab with a box to add a domain and the DNS records to add at your domain company.
shot.caption: Add your domain, then copy the two records to your domain company.

bullets.0: DNS changes usually show up within minutes, but can take a few hours. Press Check now again later.
bullets.1: The check says which record it can't find yet: the TXT record, or the one that points your domain here.
bullets.2: Some domain companies add your domain to the end of the name by themselves. If yours does, type only the first part of the name, like www or _verify.www.
bullets.3: For an address without www (yourbusiness.com), some domain companies don't allow a CNAME record. Use an A record pointing to this server's IP address instead; ask whoever runs {app} for you for the address.

body.0: Press the bin next to the domain and confirm. Your app stays at its free address.

bullets.0: A domain can only be connected to one app.
bullets.1: Your plan may limit how many domains you can connect.
bullets.2: Visitors see your published app at your domain, so publish before you share it.

phone-apps.title: Phone apps and notifications
phone-apps.summary: Your app as a real phone app: try it on your phone, send notifications, and build it for Google Play and the App Store.

0.heading: Add it to a home screen

body.0: Every published app can be installed straight from the browser, with no app store. Open your app on the phone (scan the code on the Overview or the Publish tab), then choose Add to Home Screen in the browser's menu. On an iPhone it's under the Share button. It then opens like any other app, with your icon.
body.1: Set your app's icon on the Overview under App icon. You can upload a picture or have the AI make one.

steps.0: Open the Notifications tab.
steps.1: If notifications are off, press Turn on notifications. This adds a small “Get notified” page your visitors use to sign up.
steps.2: Publish your app so visitors can sign up.
steps.3: Write a Title and a Message. You can add a page to open when the notification is tapped, like /menu.
steps.4: Press Send to (it shows how many people will get it). Sent lists what you've sent and how many were delivered.

shot.alt: The Notifications tab with the number of subscribers and a form to write and send a notification.
shot.caption: Write a notification and send it to everyone who signed up.

body.0: On Android phones and computers, people turn on notifications from the browser. On iPhone and iPad, they first add your app to their home screen, then turn on notifications there.
body.1: Flows can send notifications too, with the Send a notification step.

3.heading: Your app as a real phone app

body.0: Every published app is also a real phone app. It is drawn with the phone's own text, buttons and lists, so it feels like any other app, not like a website in a frame. It is made from your published app, and every time you publish, phones that have it get the new version the next time they open it. No new store version is needed.
body.1: Open the Mobile app tab. Your phone app shows it in a phone you can tap and scroll. Choose the Page, an iPhone or Android phone, Light or Dark, and, if your app has more than one language, the Language. Turn on Compare with web to see your website next to it.

shot.alt: The Mobile app tab with the phone app shown in an iPhone, and buttons to choose the page, the phone and light or dark.
shot.caption: Your phone app, live, in an iPhone or Android phone.

body.0: Under Does it look the same?, press Check this page or Check all pages. Each page gets Looks the same, Looks close or Looks different. Side by side shows your website, the phone app and the differences in red, so you can spot anything that came out differently.
body.1: Almost everything is drawn natively. A few things, like maps and videos from other websites, drawings and parts with their own code, are shown in a small embedded web view instead. Which parts run as embedded web views, and why lists them for each page. They still work and look like your website.

body.0: See your app on your own phone in seconds, before building anything.

steps.0: Install the free Expo Go app from the App Store or Google Play.
steps.1: On the Mobile app tab, under Try it on your phone, scan the code. On an iPhone, use the Camera app; on Android, use the scanner inside Expo Go.
steps.2: Your app opens. This preview is only for you; your customers get the real app from the stores.

shot.alt: The Try it on your phone section with a code to scan and three short steps.
shot.caption: Scan the code with your phone to try your app.

body.0: On some servers you can also press Start an Android phone under Try it in your browser (Android): a real Android phone appears right in the page and you use your app with your mouse and keyboard. It turns off by itself after 10 minutes without anyone looking at it. If you don't see this section, your server doesn't offer it.
Under Build for the app stores, Android apps are built for you on the server.

steps.0: Publish your app first.
steps.1: Under App details, check the App name, the Bundle / Application ID (like com.yourbusiness.app; never change it once your app is in a store), Version, Orientation and colours, then press Save settings.
steps.2: Press Build test app for a copy you can install straight on an Android phone to try it. Download it on the phone and open it.
steps.3: When you're ready for Google Play, press Build for Google Play and upload the file it makes. Put your app on Google Play walks you through the store's steps.

shot.alt: The Build for the app stores section with buttons to build a test app and the file for Google Play.
shot.caption: Build a test app, or the file Google Play asks for.

body.0: Google Play knows your app by its upload key, a secret file made the first time you build for Google Play. Press Download key backup and keep it somewhere private, like a password manager. Without it you can never update your app on Google Play again. Only the app's owner can download it.

Apple only lets iPhone apps be built with its own tools, on a Mac. Press Download iPhone project and either open it in Xcode on a Mac, or, without a Mac, put it in a free GitHub account and let GitHub build it and send it to TestFlight. Both need a paid Apple Developer account. The README inside the download explains every step.
body.1: Your iPhone app updates itself when you publish, like the Android one. You only need a new iPhone version when its name, icon or phone features change.

body.0: When someone who installed your app taps a link to your app's address, the app can open instead of the browser. This works on your own domain (connect one on the Domains tab), not on the shared address. Android is set up for you after your first build; if you publish on Google Play, also paste the Google Play app signing key (SHA-256) from Play Console. For iPhone, enter your Apple Team ID under iPhone and iPad.

bullets.0: After you press Publish, the Publish tab says Phone app updated once the phone app has the new version.
bullets.1: Phone features this app uses lists what your app asks the phone for, like the camera or location. When that list changes, build again and send the stores the new version.
bullets.2: Apps built before the phone app existed show your website inside an app frame. They keep working, and you can still build them under Classic (website) app at the bottom of the tab.
bullets.3: Phones only open apps from a secure address (https). The Mobile app tab warns you if yours isn't.
bullets.4: If it says builds are turned off on this server, ask whoever runs {app} for you.
bullets.5: Before deleting an app or your account, download its Google Play upload key.

account-and-billing.title: Your profile, plan and settings
account-and-billing.summary: Add a photo, change your name and password, choose light or dark, turn help tips on or off, check your plan and AI use, or delete your account.

steps.0: Click your picture (or initial) at the top right, then Profile.
steps.1: Press Add a photo and pick a picture of you. It's cropped to a square and shows next to your name. Change photo or Remove it any time.
steps.2: Change your Name and press Save. Your email is the one you sign in with and can't be changed here.
steps.3: Under Password, type your Current password and a New password of at least 8 characters, then press Change password. You're signed out on your other devices.

shot.alt: The Profile page with your photo, details, password, appearance and help tips.
shot.caption: Profile: your photo, name, password, light or dark, and help tips.

body.0: If you don't know your current password, for example because you signed up with Google, sign out and use Forgot password on the sign-in page to set one.

Press the sun or moon button in the top bar to switch between light and dark. In your Profile, under Appearance, you can also choose Match my device, which follows your computer or phone. Your choice is saved to your account, so it follows you to other devices.
Help tips are short notes that appear when you hold your mouse over a button or setting. Turn them on or off in your Profile under Help. Inside an app, the Help tips button at the top does the same.
body.1: The Help link in the top bar opens the guide for the screen you're on. Help & guides in the account menu lists every guide.

body.0: Click your initial, then Billing & plan. It shows your plan and, if your plan has a monthly allowance, how many AI actions you've used this month. Planning, building and changing things with the AI all use AI actions.
body.1: When they run out, the AI pauses until next month. Templates and the page editor keep working. If other plans are offered, you can pick one on the same page. Once you pay for a plan, Manage billing lets you change your payment details.

shot.alt: The Billing page showing your plan and the AI actions you've used this month.
shot.caption: Billing & plan: your plan and this month's AI use.

body.0: This deletes your account and all your apps, with everything they saved, their files and their web addresses. It can't be undone.

steps.0: Go to your Profile and find Delete my account.
steps.1: Download a Backup of each app you might want later. If an app is on Google Play, download its Google Play upload key too.
steps.2: Press Delete my account….
steps.3: Type your email address to confirm, and tick the upload key box if it's shown.

bullets.0: Changing your password signs you out everywhere else.
bullets.1: A paid plan is cancelled straight away when you delete your account.
bullets.2: If your account can't be deleted here, for example because you run a workspace for other people, your Profile page explains why.

running-your-platform.title: Running your platform
running-your-platform.summary: Your admin home: set up {app}, look after the people using it, and keep the server healthy.

body.0: Click Admin in the top bar. Run your platform has a card for each area, with how it stands now: White-label branding, Resellers, Payments, Plans & limits, AI engine, Email, Users and System. Click a card to open it. All settings at the top opens every setting on one page.

shot.alt: The Admin home with cards for branding, resellers, payments, plans, AI, email, users and system, and a setup checklist.
shot.caption: The Admin home: every area of the platform, and what still needs doing.

body.0: The Setup checklist ticks itself off as you go. Click a step to open its setting.

steps.0: Set your brand: your name, logo and colours. See Your brand (white-label).
steps.1: Connect an AI engine, so people can build by describing their app. See AI settings.
steps.2: Connect Stripe and price your plans, if you charge. See Prices and payments.
steps.3: Turn on email, so invitations, password links and alerts are sent for you. See Email.
steps.4: Give published apps their own address. This is a server setting (APPS_DOMAIN in the .env file), not on this screen; the installer can set it. With a wildcard DNS record, every published app gets its own address, kept apart from the studio.
steps.5: Invite your first reseller, if you sell through agencies. See Resellers and clients.

body.0: Under All settings, Plans & limits sets what Free, Starter, Pro and Team include: Apps, Published apps, Pages per app, Custom domains, AI actions / month and Scheduled workflows. Tick unlimited for no limit, then press Save plan limits. Reset to the standard limits puts back the built-in values. You and your resellers are never limited.
The Users list on the Admin home shows everyone who signed up. For each person you can:

bullets.0: Change their plan from the menu. It saves straight away.
bullets.1: Press Password link to make a sign-in link that works once, for 2 hours. It's emailed to them if email is on, or copied for you to send.
bullets.2: Press Impersonate to open their workspace and help them. A banner shows while you're inside, and anything you change happens in their account. Press Stop impersonating to come back.
bullets.3: Press Delete to delete their account. You'll see what goes with it and type their email to confirm.

body.0: New people, last 30 days shows how many people signed up, made an app and published one. Recent projects lists the latest apps, with Jump in to open one in its owner's workspace. Recent flow runs shows the latest automations and whether they worked.

Open System for the server's health in plain words. Each check is a card: green is fine, amber could use a look, red needs attention now. It covers the database, disk space, scheduled flows, backups, email, the AI connection, memory and more.
body.1: Nightly clean-up removes old run logs, expired sign-ins, old published versions and the files of deleted apps. Choose Report only (count, delete nothing), Remove old records or Off, and press Save. Check now or Run clean-up now runs it straight away. Take a backup before you first turn on removing: deleted records can't be brought back.
body.2: If something goes wrong, Details for support copies or downloads a summary with private details hidden, ready to send to whoever supports you.

shot.alt: The System page: a summary line, health check cards, and the nightly clean-up settings.
shot.caption: System: how the server is doing, in plain words.

bullets.0: If the database needs an update after you upgrade, a banner at the top of the Admin home says so, and System explains what to do.
bullets.1: Installs made with the standard installer back themselves up every night. Copy the backups to another device now and then.
bullets.2: Monitoring tools can check /api/health to see that the server is up.
bullets.3: The operator's runbook in the download (docs/operations.md) covers the details.

white-label.title: Your brand (white-label)
white-label.summary: Put your own name, logo and colours on the studio, its emails and its sign-in pages.

body.0: The platform's operator sets the brand everyone sees by default. Each reseller sets their own brand, and their clients only ever see that one, never the platform's.
body.1: If you run the platform: go to Admin, All settings, Branding.
body.2: If you're a reseller: open your Reseller dashboard and choose Branding.

steps.0: Type your Brand name. It's shown at the top of every screen, in emails and on the sign-in page.
steps.1: Add a Tagline (optional), a short line about what you offer. It's added to the browser tab's title.
steps.2: Upload a Logo. Wide logos look best; use PNG or SVG, under 150 KB. It's shown instead of the brand name.
steps.3: Upload a Browser icon: square, at least 64 by 64 pixels.
steps.4: Pick a Main colour (buttons and highlights) and an Accent colour (smaller touches).
steps.5: Add a Support email. It's shown to people who need help and used as the reply-to address on emails. Add Your website if you like.
steps.6: Check the Preview of the sign-in screen, then press Save branding.

shot.alt: The White-label branding form with name, tagline, logo, icon, colours and support email, and a preview of the sign-in screen.
shot.caption: Your brand, with a live preview of the sign-in screen.

body.0: Your clients can sign in and build at an address you own, like apps.youragency.com. Their published apps are shared from it too.

steps.0: In your Reseller dashboard, open Domain.
steps.1: Type a subdomain you control, like apps.youragency.com, and press Use this domain.
steps.2: Add the two records shown (a CNAME or A record, and a TXT record) where you manage your domain's DNS.
steps.3: Press Check now. When it says Connected, your clients can sign in there.

bullets.0: Changes show the next time a page loads.
bullets.1: Images over 150 KB are refused. Export a smaller version and try again.
bullets.2: A reseller's address gets a secure (https) certificate by itself on servers set up for it. If it doesn't open securely, ask the platform's operator.
bullets.3: To stop using a reseller address, clear the box and save.
bullets.4: Operators: give published apps a neutral address (APPS_DOMAIN) so reseller clients' app links don't show the platform's name.

resellers.title: Resellers and clients
resellers.summary: Sell app building under another brand: the operator adds resellers, and each reseller invites and looks after their own clients.

bullets.0: The operator runs the platform and sets the plans, prices and limits.
bullets.1: Resellers are agencies the operator adds. Each has its own brand, address, Stripe account and clients.
bullets.2: Clients are the reseller's customers. They build apps and only ever see the reseller's brand.
bullets.3: App users are the people who use the published apps.
bullets.4: Clients pay the reseller directly. The platform takes no cut.

steps.0: In Admin, open Resellers.
steps.1: Under Add a reseller, type the Brand name, the Reseller's email and, if you like, Their name.
steps.2: Set Max clients, Max apps and AI actions / month, or leave them empty for unlimited.
steps.3: Press Create reseller. They get an invitation email if email is set up; otherwise you get a link to send them.

shot.alt: The Resellers page with a form to add a reseller and a table of resellers with their clients, apps and AI use.
shot.caption: Add resellers and set their limits.

body.0: The table shows each reseller's clients, apps, AI actions this month, domain and status. Click a number like 3 / 10 to change that limit. The buttons at the end of a row let you sign in as the reseller, make an invitation or password reset link, suspend or reactivate them, and delete them.
body.1: The monthly AI limit covers the reseller and all their clients together. When it runs out, the AI pauses for all of them until next month. The reseller is emailed at 80% and 100%, if email is set up.
body.2: Suspending a reseller signs out the reseller and all their clients. Deleting one asks you to type its name; its clients keep their accounts and apps and become your direct customers on the Free plan.

body.0: Click Reseller dashboard in the top bar. Overview has a Get set up checklist (logo and colours, your own domain, payments, your first client) and how many clients, apps and AI actions you're using. The menu on the left has Clients, Apps, Branding, Domain and Billing & plans.

steps.0: Open Clients.
steps.1: Under Invite a client, type their Email, their Name if you like, and choose their Plan.
steps.2: Press Send invite. They get an email with a link to set their password, or you get the link to send if email isn't set up.
steps.3: To invite lots of people, press Invite several at once and paste up to 50 email addresses.

body.0: The client list shows each client's status, plan, apps, AI use and when they were last active. Filter it by status, plan and payment, or tick Not seen in 30 days or Never signed in. Needs attention points out clients who may need a nudge.
body.1: Change a client's plan from the menu in their row. The buttons in each row let you Open their workspace (press Back to your clients to return), send a new invitation or password reset link, suspend or restore their access, and delete them.
body.2: Deleting a client deletes all their apps. You'll be asked to type their email to confirm.

body.0: Apps lists every app your clients have made. Press Open to edit one in the client's workspace. Apps you built yourself have Give to client, which moves the app to a client's workspace; you can still open it for them.

bullets.0: A reseller only sees their own clients, never the operator's other customers or settings.
bullets.1: Clients sign in at the reseller's address and see only the reseller's brand.
bullets.2: When you've used all your client seats, invitations stop until the operator adds more.

prices-and-payments.title: Prices and payments
prices-and-payments.summary: Connect Stripe, and set what each plan costs and includes, so customers pay you directly.

body.0: If you run the platform: Admin, All settings, then Payments for prices and Stripe, and Plans & limits for what each plan includes.
body.1: If you're a reseller: your Reseller dashboard, Billing & plans. It has 1. Your prices and 2. What each plan includes.
body.2: Payments go through Stripe, an online payment service. You need your own Stripe account.

steps.0: In Stripe, go to Developers, API keys, and copy the Secret key. To try things out first, use a test key (it starts sk_test_).
steps.1: Paste it into Secret key under Stripe.
steps.2: Press Save prices. {app} sets up the payment updates from Stripe for you.

steps.0: Under Plans and prices, each paid plan has a Plan name, a Price per month and a Currency.
steps.1: Type a price for each plan you want to offer. Leave a price empty to hide that plan. The Free plan is always there.
steps.2: Press Save prices. The prices are created in your Stripe account for you.

shot.alt: The Payments section with a name, monthly price and currency for each paid plan, and the Stripe key.
shot.caption: Name and price each plan, and connect Stripe.

body.0: For each plan, set the number of Apps, Published apps, Pages per app, Custom domains and AI actions / month, and whether Scheduled workflows are included.
body.1: On the operator's Plans & limits, tick unlimited for no limit, then press Save plan limits. On a reseller's Billing & plans, leave a box empty for unlimited and press Save plans.
body.2: Resellers can also untick Let new clients sign themselves up on your domain to make accounts invitation-only.

shot.alt: The Plans and limits table, with a column for each plan and a row for each limit.
shot.caption: What each plan includes.

body.0: Customers see the plans you offer on their Billing & plan page, with an Upgrade button that takes them to Stripe to pay. Paying customers get Manage billing to change their card or cancel. Until Stripe is connected, your prices still show, and checkout works once it's connected.
body.1: You can also change someone's plan by hand: the operator from the Users list, a reseller from the client list.

bullets.0: Customers pay you directly, on your own Stripe account. The platform takes no fee.
bullets.1: If Stripe's payment updates ever fail to set up, Advanced: payment updates (webhook) shows the address to add in Stripe by hand.
bullets.2: Try everything with a Stripe test key before you switch to your live key.

ai-settings.title: AI settings
ai-settings.summary: Choose the AI engine that plans, builds and changes apps, and check that it works.

body.0: In Admin, open All settings and go to AI engine. Until an engine is connected, building with AI is off: people start from templates and the page editor, and the AI Designer can't build.
There are two options:

bullets.0: OpenAI: OpenAI's service, or any server that works the same way, including models running on your own hardware.
bullets.1: Command-line AI agent: a command-line AI tool installed on this server, signed in with its own subscription, instead of paying per request.

shot.alt: The AI provider settings with the two provider options, the connection details and a test button.
shot.caption: Pick a provider, fill in its details and test it.

2.heading: Connect a hosted or compatible service

steps.0: Choose OpenAI.
steps.1: Paste your key into OpenAI / compatible API key. If a key is already stored, leave the box empty to keep it.
steps.2: Leave API base URL empty for OpenAI's own service, or type the address of a compatible server.
steps.3: Type the model names under Scaffold model (plans and builds new apps) and Edit model (changes in the editor), or leave them empty for the defaults.
steps.4: Press Test connection. It saves your settings first, then shows OK or Failed with the reason.

3.heading: Run the AI on your own hardware

body.0: Any model server that speaks the same language as OpenAI's service works, such as Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or llama.cpp's server. Put its address in API base URL (for a model on the same computer as {app}'s Docker containers, something like http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1), leave the key empty unless the server needs one, and type the model's exact name.
body.1: Leave Model context size and Maximum output tokens per call empty, and Model thinking on Automatic: {app} works out sensible values. If tests or builds say the answer was unreadable, set JSON support to Prompt only.
body.2: Speed depends on your hardware. Bigger models write better pages; try building a sample app before you invite people.

steps.0: Install the tool on this server and sign it in, as the account that runs {app} (or its dedicated runner account).
steps.1: Choose Command-line AI agent.
steps.2: Set Model if you want a different one, and Binary path only if the tool isn't found by itself.
steps.3: Press Test the AI agent, then Save changes.

bullets.0: Every plan, build and change uses AI actions from the person's monthly allowance (see Plans & limits), and a reseller's clients share the reseller's monthly limit.
bullets.1: Stored keys are never shown again, only a masked hint.
bullets.2: A key in the server's .env file (OPENAI_API_KEY) is used when none is saved here.
bullets.3: The runbook in the download (docs/local-ai.md) has more on running models yourself.

email.title: Email
email.summary: Send invitations, password links, app alerts and your apps' own emails from your own address.

body.0: Once email is set up, {app} sends password links and invitations (for you, resellers and their clients), alerts to app owners when someone sends a form or books, and the emails apps send themselves with the Send an email step.
body.1: Without it, invitation and password links are shown on screen for you to pass on, and apps skip their email steps. App owners see a note about it on their app's Overview.

1.heading: Set it up with any email provider

steps.0: In Admin, open All settings and go to Email.
steps.1: Under How should email be sent?, choose Any email provider (SMTP).
steps.2: Type the Email server your provider gives you, like smtp.example.com.
steps.3: Choose the Port. Use 587 (recommended) unless your provider says otherwise.
steps.4: Type the Username and Password. Google and Microsoft need an app password, not your normal one.
steps.5: Type the address to Send from, one your provider lets you send from, and a Sender name if you like. Leave the name empty to use your brand's or the app's name.
steps.6: Press Send a test email to me. It uses what's on screen, so you can check before saving.

shot.alt: The Email settings: whether email is on, the choice of provider, the server details and the test button.
shot.caption: Fill in your provider's details and send yourself a test.

body.0: Choose Resend, paste your Resend API key, and send from an address on a domain you've verified in Resend. Then test and save as above.

The box at the top says Email is on with the address it sends from, and shows the last 24 hours: how many were sent and failed, and the last problem, if any. The Email card on the System page shows the same.

bullets.0: Username or password rejected: check both. Google and Microsoft need an app password; email services often give you an SMTP key instead of your account password.
bullets.1: Couldn't reach the server on that port: try 587, then 465, then 2525, or ask your host to open the port.
bullets.2: The port and encryption don't match: use 465 with SSL, or 587 with automatic encryption (under More options).
bullets.3: Refused to send from that address: your provider hasn't verified that sender or its domain. Verify it, or send from an address it knows.
bullets.4: Resend's test mode: a new Resend account only emails its own address until you verify a domain.

bullets.0: Every email is sent from your Send from address. When an app asks to send from an address on another domain, its address becomes the reply-to, so replies still reach the app owner.
bullets.1: Settings in the server's .env file are used until you save here; saving here takes over.
bullets.2: Remove these settings goes back to no email (or to the .env settings, if there are any).
bullets.3: The support email in your branding is the reply-to on invitation and password emails.
